blind_spots.blind_spot: The signature library is simultaneously the business model and a controlled artifact the customer will not let them keep
blind_spots.operator_reality: A cross-customer database of golden electrical signatures for mission-critical microelectronics is a map of which parts sit in which weapon systems, in what volumes, and where the sourcing is thin — which is exactly what an adversary supply-chain analyst wants. A defense customer will class that as CUI at minimum, require NIST 800-171/CMMC handling, and in many programs insist the library live inside their boundary with no cross-program aggregation. That guts the network effect the product is built around. The architecture answer — per-tenant enclaves, exportable signature packages, a federated comparison that never centralizes raw data — is cheap to design now and a rewrite once a prime's security team reads the data flow.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: In commercial high-reliability electronics a shared reference library is a pure asset and the more customers contribute, the better it gets, so the incentive has always pointed toward centralization.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: The Chiplytics desktop app automates data collection and stores signatures locally or over a secure cloud database for scalable data management and analysis.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Testing to AS6171 is not the same as being an accepted test house
blind_spots.operator_reality: Under DFARS 252.246-7007 and -7008 the prime, not the vendor, owns the counterfeit detection and avoidance system and must source from approved suppliers; a test result only counts if it comes from a lab the prime and the program office recognize, typically ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation scoped to AS6171 and a place on an approved-source list. Without that, a prime treats Chiplytics data as advisory and re-tests anyway, which caps the deal at pilot size forever. There is also an obligation nobody has named: when a part is judged suspect counterfeit, someone has to file a GIDEP report, and whether that is the customer or the lab is a contractual term that should be settled before the first finding, not after.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The STTR is a technology-development vehicle with a university partner, so the work is judged on whether the method discriminates parts — accreditation and reporting duties live in an acquisition and quality-assurance world the research contract never touches.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Quality is financially guaranteed through our extended warranty and backed by reporting on our platform.

blind_spots.blind_spot: One hundred percent coverage is a fixturing problem, not an algorithm problem
blind_spots.operator_reality: The differentiator claimed is screening every component rather than a sample, but the interface is a 40-pin ZIF socket plus per-package socket adapters. Real depot and prime incoming inspection means lots of thousands of parts spanning dozens of package types, including high-pin-count BGAs and QFNs where a test socket is a custom part with weeks of lead time and a four-figure price. At transition the question is throughput per shift and cost per part against a sample-based baseline, and the answer is set by socket tooling and handler automation — the least glamorous part of the system and the one a six-person team is least resourced to industrialize.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The STTR demonstration set is chosen to prove discrimination on representative parts, so package diversity looks like a catalog problem rather than the dominant cost driver it becomes at volume.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Electronic components interface with the 40-pin zero insertion force (ZIF) socket or low leadtime socket adapters manufactured by Chiplytics for a wide range of package types.

opener_hook: Your PSA app stores component signatures 'locally or over a secure cloud database', and the AFWERX STTR you are on with CALCE (FA864924P1109) will eventually make that library CUI — at which point where it lives matters more than how well it discriminates parts.
what_they_do: Six-person Seattle startup detecting counterfeit and degraded microelectronics by capturing patented power-spectrum electrical fingerprints of every part, sold as inspection hardware plus a sourcing-and-certification service.
